title: Harrison Goodell
description: Harrison Goodell – Tough Love Tour One of the Northeast’s top emerging artists, Harrison Goodell brings his full band to The Rockwell for a night of indie folk and Americana. With new material on the way and sessions in Nashville with some of the industry’s most exciting writers, 2026 is set to be a defining year. title: bellwire
description: bellwire SHOW DESCRIPTION: bellwire return to Boston with a new song in their bittersweet register tackling love, existence, and entropy. “LOVEBIRDS” (featuring a fellow sweet prince of New England songcraft, Jake McKelvie, singing harmony). The song will come out on the morning of the show. Since frontman Tyler berd’s move to the west coast, the full bellwire is at most a twice-a-year sighting in these haunts. Don’t sleep on this, especially with their roadworn pirate pedal-steel player Jonee Earthquake at the slide and pedals. They will be joined by two local favorites: Yes, Chef and Mel Starr and the Astral Projection. bellwire: bellwire is a New England rock band first formed in the summer of 2011, now most commonly spotted in the fall. Early experiments in lo-fi, surf, and punk gave way to their jangly power-pop style typified on the EP, Dog Thoughts . Their self-titled 2022 LP is an alt-country concept album that tells a story of love and loss (single: Dreamin’ ). Often appearing with New England pirate-punk stalwart Jonee Earthquake on pedal steel, their high-energy performances still put lyrics and story first. LINKS: Bandcamp / Tidal / Apple / S potify / Instagram / Facebook Mel Starr: Based out of Boston, MA, Mel Starr is a self-taught singer/songwriter inspired by the folk tradition and the fingerpicking style. With no formal music education, intuition is deeply integrated into their music practice. Mel’s songs are soothing and, at times, haunting. They reflect on family, grief, relationships and finding oneself in their writing. Mel cares deeply about mental health and community wellbeing, using music as a path to bring people together in learning and collaboration. In their opinion, it is one of life’s true pleasures to see how a song can transform when instruments and minds conspire to create something new. title: Hippies & Cowboys w Velvet Daydream
description: Hippies & Cowboys with Velvet Daydream Hippies And Cowboys are a powerhouse rock ’n’ soul band out of Nashville, TN, built on grit, groove, and the raw electricity of classic Southern rock—revived with a modern edge. Their sound fuses deep-pocket soul, blues, and rock ’n’ roll, channeling icons such as Aerosmith, The Allman Brothers, Tedeschi Trucks and others. Rooted in tradition and sharpened by the road, Hippies And Cowboys cut their early recordings in legendary rooms including FAME Studios, Muscle Shoals Sound, and East Avalon—capturing the same spirit that shaped generations of American music. Their debut release, Live at Fox and Locke (2023), bottled the raw, no-holds-barred energy of their live show and quickly earned critical acclaim. The follow-up EP, Fork in the Road (2024), doubled down with a gritty, hard-hitting collection of songs that showcased their deep Southern roots, tight musicianship, and fearless songwriting. A live double album and full concert film are slated for release in 2026. title: Abby Holliday, Charli Adams
description: Abby Holliday + Charli Adams There comes a time in every artist’s career when the art form transcends a mere outlet for self-expression and becomes a universal gift to mankind. For some it takes years, for Abby Holliday it was there from the start. Her vulnerable introspection and brutal lyricism combined with mind-bending sonic sensibilities and a distinct production style immediately fused a bond between her and her loyal fan base. Holliday masterfully guides listeners through moments in time extremely specific to her own life that puts words to collective experiences of the human condition, reaching into places we might not have known existed prior. Abby found her voice during her early years of college where she began quietly writing songs in the confines of her room. After a friend heard the songs and encouraged her to share them, Abby met producer Jonathan Class and set off to record her debut album WHEN WE’RE FAR APART I FALL APART. It was in these studio moments where Abby’s sound began to take shape, a launchpad for her sophomore album I’M OK NO I’M NOT. Holliday and Class experiment with a wide range of sounds from vocoded vocal stacks, to jarring synths, to lush strings and piano, to a tasteful blend of organic and synthetic rhythm sections amassing in a discography that runs the gambit of the most beautiful songs to songs that smack you in the face with unforgettable hooks and driving beats. CRACK A SMILE COME ON STAY A WHILE, Holliday’s highly anticipated junior record, is out now. “Former cheer captain” isn’t something you always see on the resume of a rising, alternative singer-songwriter. For Charli Adams, who grew up across several small towns in rural Alabama, an outward display of optimism might have been the only way to get by. title: The Darkness Behind
description: The Darkness Behind SHOW DESCRIPTION: The Darkness Behind is a solo multimedia performance that explores the many meanings behind the title: surviving darkness, leaving darkness behind, and the ongoing tension between memory and freedom. Ameen’s musical journey during the ISIS occupation of his hometown in Iraq, Mosul, 2014-2017, and the musical chapters post that period. Using violin, voice, live looping, and electronic textures, the performance combines cinematic music, experimental sound, and personal storytelling that creates an immersive live experience. This work follows performances at venues including The Metropolitan Museum of Art and One World Trade Center. ARTIST BIO: Award-winning Iraqi composer, performer, and multidisciplinary artist, born In Baghdad 1989. Ameen’s work across film, theater, and contemporary music, and he is internationally active collaborator with ensembles and institutions in the U.S., Middle, East, and Europe. title: Kooked Out, Viper Cut Eyes, Stunt
description: Kooked Out, Viper Cut Eyes, Stunt SHOW DESCRIPTION: The Scene Within the Scene is a local community building platform for artists and musicians to connect and support one another. This is the first show curated by this group which is completely non profit. The bands on this first show are High Energy Rock bands with influences from Garage/Surf Punk/ and Psych Rock. ARTIST BIOS: Kooked Out: “The kaleidoscopic sound of Kooked Out has evolved naturally throughout the years and draws influences from almost every genre and decade of music from the 1930s to present day, crafting a unique mix of styles and sounds that have developed Kooked Out a cult-like following in the skate and surf communities. Leaning heavily into the music of the ’50s, ’60s and early 2000s, Kooked Out’s genre-spanning sound has become a calling card, both on record and live on stage, appropriate for a creative outlet that lists its top influences as The White Stripes, The Beatles, Jimi Hendrix, Dick Dale, The Black Keys, Cage The Elephant, and Blink-182.” -Michael Marotta / Knyvet Members: John Fiore, Chris Laskey, Chris Caduto, Emily Trubey / ‘2024 Live Act Of The Year’ New England Music Awards Viper Cut Eyes: Boston’s unapologetically noisy and transcendent Surfadelic Psych Rock unit Ace McGuire’s Acid Tabs are defibrillating stagnant bodies with blood pulsing riffs paired with a hit of tape echoed and verbed out psychedelia. Originally a bedroom recording project of Bermudian singer and songwriter Liv Dunks and New Bedford MA’s guitarist, singer and producer Mitch Cardoza, they expanded their vision by adding San Francisco’s multi-instrumentalist Erik Dietz on bass. Stunt!: Brings the attitude and aggression of 90s Rock bands to today’s pop music scene. Riffs inspired by the grunge and pop-punk sounds of yesterday meld with vocal melodies that hang with any of today’s radio ear worms. Social Medias: @thescenewithinthescene / @kookedoutofficial / @viper.cut.eyes / @thebandstunt DOORS: 7:00 PM SHOW

title: Nelward
description: Nelward nelward is an innovative music artist creating funky electronic artpop for the internet age. Early on, the melodies of classic Nintendo games were etched into his ADHD brain and never seemed to leave. Drawing from a wide array of influences, nelward enjoys the explorative aspect of music creation and is not one to dwell in one sound for too long. He is also known for the colorful and whimsical art direction in his often self-produced videos. In 2017, his first EP Alive in Screen established his foundational sound. The subsequent success of the new jack swing/nu metal banger Ghost / Getting Better and bubblegum pop earworm Never Wanna Fall in Love With U established him as a force to be reckoned with in the independent electronic music scene. 2020’s Eat Your Dreams EP delved into heavier subject matter while tightening nelward’s knack for catchy songwriting. 2024’s single THE RUNAROUND combines infectious earworms while embracing musical exploration. Nelward is known for his animated live performances, completing a 40+ date tour of North America and Europe with TWRP from 2024-2025. In 2025 the nelward live band was born, representing a distinct chapter in the evolution of his live performance. Nelward represents a growing segment of independent electronic artists who are building significant followings through digital platforms while creating innovative multimedia art experiences. Justice Cow is the cosmic gumbo of Jessica Kion. She grew up in a musical family which meant pressing rewind until she had transcribed every word of the “Grease” soundtrack and being forced to sing barbershop quartet family-style in the car. For over a decade she has toured extensively across the US and abroad, equally at home in living rooms, rock clubs, and festival stages. title: Julia Minkin
description: Julia Minkin SHOW DESCRIPTION: Chicago-based singer-songwriter Julia Minkin is joined by Boston favorites Bowling Shoes and Cate Yoder for an evening of inventive indie music, compelling storytelling, and rich, genre-bending sounds. From shimmering synth-pop and art-rock experimentation to intimate folk melodies, this lineup offers music that’s as intelligent as it is fun. ARTIST BIOS: Julia Minken: Best known for co-writing viral hit songs with French electropop sensation Kid Francescoli, Chicago-based singer-songwriter Julia Minkin steps into her own with her debut album Not Ready, co-created and produced with her husband Andrew Sudhibhasilp. Blending warm, folk-tinged vocals with nostalgic dance-floor energy and introspection, Minkin “finds her own creative voice, shimmering, rhythmic, and heartfelt—both bold and refreshingly sincere” (Thoughts Words Actions). Bowling Shoes: Melding innovative art-pop experimentalism with indie-rock nuance and arena-ready hooks, Boston, MA’s Bowling Shoes craft eminently catchy music sprinkled with delightful touches of subversive noise Cate Yoder: A double and electric bassist and guitarist from Richmond, Virginia, Cate Yoder learns about her environment through exploring, inventing, and performing a multitude of genres or really any music she can get hands on. Since being established primarily as a bass player, she is diving into the songwriting indie folk role with her band of talented women, performing in the Boston area. With airy melodies, detailed guitar, piano, and percussive elements, and bitter lyrics, she hopes to share her experience of finding solace and comfort in a complex world. title: GHOSTWOMAN
description: GHOSTWOMAN GHOSTWOMAN itself only exists because Uschenko and van Dessel were the ones “stupid enough to commit to it”. Conceived by Uschenko after cutting his teeth as a touring multi-instrumentalist, the project was brought to life in an abandoned farmhouse in Diamond City, Alberta. There, for two months, he would make the self-released, self-titled debut album which was produced and dubbed directly to custom-made cassette tapes. The music has always been beautifully inhospitable, earned only by those curious enough to seek it out. — Dine Alone Records Presented by Get To The Gig & MassConcerts Ages: Show age differs by the day. title: Summer Reading Brewery Book Fair
description: Free RSVP Here Calling all beer and book lovers: stock up for your summer reading at our CX taproom scholastic book fair! Just in time for summer reading! Join us at the Cambridge Crossing taproom to relive the joy and wonder of a Scholastic Book Fair. We're teaming up with More Than Words, a local bookstore and nonprofit, to bring you the nostalgia of the book fair with a local flair, more age-appropriate books for adults, and curated book & beer pairings! At More Than Words, youth ages 16-24 who are in foster care, experiencing homelessness, out-of-school, or in the court system, learn to run an online and retail bookstore while also getting full wrap-around supports to tackle the barriers from our state systems and take charge of their lives. Each purchase from the book fair will support this mission! Browse the stacks, grab a beer, and chat with other book lovers!

description: Every other month, we team up with the Cambridge Public Library to highlight contemporary works from marginalized voices. All over a fresh, craft beer, of course! For May, we plan on reading Death of the Soccer God by Dimitry Elias Leger - a passionate and improbable love story, and a roaring Pan-American tale about the price of fame. We’ll gather in person in our Broadway location’s back taproom on Wednesday, July 1st, at 7:00 pm for our monthly discussion. Grab a beer, cold brew, or kombucha at the front bar, then come find us in the back. The discussion is casual, and all are welcome – even if you don’t finish the book, we’d still love to have you. Copies of the book are available at the Main Library in Cambridge, at 449 Broadway. The e-book and digital audiobook can be borrowed through the Libby app. Let us know if you need help accessing the book. Please note that our taprooms are 21+ and all guests should be prepared to show a valid, current government-issued photo ID at the door. Questions? Get in touch: events@lamplighterbrewing.com

title: Pepita Lo-Fi Friday
description: Lo-Fi Fridays are here! Just like our Lo-Fi weekends but now during the work week! Stop by the “secret” back taproom of our sweet little cafe space every Friday morning for a quiet sanctuary of productivity and peace. Need a bit of quiet time? The Lamplighter + Pepita team are here to bring you a little slice of calm. From here on out, we will open the back taproom from 8am-2pm on Friday mornings for Lo Fi Fridays. Think of it as a designated calming, quiet zone just for our Pepita patrons. We’ll play chill, ambient music to set the vibe, and folks are encouraged to read, work, study, etc. with minimal talking preferred. Grab a coffee and cozy up in the back taproom at our 284 Broadway location to soak up that tranquil energy or to get a jump start on the week ahead. Your weekend brunch plans have never been more relaxing! P.S. If you’re not feeling quiet time, the front taproom will remain open as usual for normal operations.

title: Broadway Trivia
description: Attend one of our most beloved, longest standing brewery traditions: Trivia Tuesday! Every Tuesday swing by our Broadway taproom for our weekly trivia night. It’s free to compete, and winners get beer money. Here’s how it works: show up with your team of 2 – 6 players starting at 7:00 pm, when we’ll open the doors to the back taproom. Head down the hallway to the back, then snag a seat. All seating is first come first serve, so we recommend arriving early – there generally is a line! The game will start at 7:30 pm, and is about two hours long (with plenty of beer breaks, of course). Questions rotate every week, and cover categories ranging from history, politics, sports, movies, pop culture, music, and more. At the end of the game, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place teams will be awarded Lamplighter gift cards – good for usage in either of our taprooms and at Pepita Coffee Co. In addition to Trivia Tuesday at our Broadway taproom, we also host weekly trivia at our CX taproom. That game takes place on Monday evenings, and is also free to join for teams of 2 – 6. We’d love to see you at either or both! Hungry? Munch on our signature giant soft pretzels or some crunchy nachos, which are available Tuesday evenings only. You’re also always welcome to bring your own food or order in, ask our staff for their favorite local recommendations. See you at trivia night! You must be 21+ attend, all guests will be asked to show valid government ID. Questions? Get in touch! You can reach us at events@lamplighterbrewing.com

title: Brewery Tour & Tasting
description: Break out your notebook and freshly sharpened No. 2 pencils because we’re going back to school! We're offering brewery tours at our original 284 Broadway location on the first Saturday of every month. Space is limited, so snag your spot right here by purchasing a ticket. Our knowledgeable team will lead you on an interactive, behind-the-scenes tour of the production floor at Lamp, where you’ll learn the essentials of craft beer-making, and how it all works at our compact, Cambridge-based facility. You'll also taste your way through the brewing process, sampling three of our current favorite draft pour picks, plus a special bonus beer to start the sipping syllabus. Will you graduate top of your class? Either way, we think you’ll find your new favorite subject. Each ticket includes: 🍻One 6 oz welcome beer, plus 3 - 5 oz flight glass-sized samples 🚶🏼A 60 min guided tasting and behind-the-scenes brewery tour 📝 Beer School "quiz" and informational answer key 📚 A Lamplighter Beer School diploma :) Questions? Get in touch! events@lamplighterbrewing.com. Please note that this event is 21+ and all guests will be asked to show a valid government-issued ID. Refund Policy We understand that plans sometimes change. If you provide us with more than 24 hours' notice prior to the event start time, we will issue a full refund to your original payment method. Within 24 hours of the start time, we will offer a refund in the form of credit to be used for a future ticketed event hosted by Lamplighter, valid for 1 year. Please note that Eventbrite fees, including processing and service fees, are nonrefundable as they are charged by Eventbrite and not under the control of Lamplighter. Please request refunds through Eventbrite, on your order confirmation page.

title: TCS presents: Shane Torres
description: 18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum.Shane Torres is a standup comedian, writer, podcaster, and actor who resides in Brooklyn. Produced by Bert and LeeAnn Kreischer, Shane’s very first special THE BLUE EYED MEXICAN was released in December 2023. Vulture named it as one of the stand-up specials not-to-be-missed in 2023, raving “The Blue Eyed Mexican, stands out for its beautiful directness and keen sense of good storytelling. It’s a refreshing combination of delicate and obscene.” It is available to stream on YouTube. Shane can be seen on CONAN (twice), THE LATE SHOW WITH STEPHEN COLBERT, NBC’S LAST COMIC STANDING, HALF HOUR SPECIAL WITH COMEDY CENTRAL, and THIS WEEK FROM THE CELLAR on Comedy Central. You might have heard Shane’s “laconic drawling delivery with deliberate pacing” as the NY Times calls it, on popular podcasts such as BERTCAST WITH BERT KREISCHER, BARSTOOL’S KFC RADIO, DR DREW AFTER DARK, THE HONEYDEW WITH RYAN SICKLER, and ARE YOU GARBAGE and a slew of others. His podcast, NO ACCOUNTING FOR TASTE with Kyle Kinane is available wherever you get your podcasts. The Bar Our Bar opens 1 hour before early shows and 20 minutes before late shows. title: Worship: Finding Meaning in Being Lost
description: Finding Meaning in Being Lost Feeling lost is a sensation we are taught from a young age to fear, a sensation that lives directly alongside turbulence and confusion. But when we are able to live safely in that state of being lost, there can be something beautiful about it. It is only in our moments of knowing the least that we can learn the most and see the world in new and unexpected ways. Join us this Sunday to explore the feeling of facing questions so deep that we don't even know where to begin. Ministerial Intern Valentin Frank preaching.

title: Gray Area: Different Eyes—Abstraction in Celtic Coins
description: This event is at capacity. Have you ever wondered why some ancient cultures do not seem as “skilled” as later societies in representing the natural world? If so, you are not alone. Many people assume that early art history is a story of technical progress toward better reproductions of reality. But what if it is less a matter of skill than of interest? Celtic coins offer a perfect opportunity to explore this idea. Join coins curator Laure Marest for this hands-on session with 2,300-year-old coins and discover the ancient Gallic fascination with abstraction. The seminar is held in conjunction with the special exhibition Celtic Art Across the Ages (March 6–August 2, 2026). This seminar is part of Gray Area, a series that features members of our curatorial staff exploring artworks that capture the complexities of humanity, political landscapes, ethics, ideologies, power dynamics, and critical thinking in our times. Through this series, we hope to encourage people to observe and consider their own individual gray areas, and to think about how their unique experiences guide the choices they make.

title: Exhibition Tour: Celtic Art Across the Ages
description: Join Christian Dupont, Boston College’s Burns Librarian, for a tour of the special exhibition Celtic Art Across the Ages. He will discuss the re-emergence of Celtic mythologies and motifs in literature and art during the 18th and 19th centuries. The so-called Celtic Revival was nourished by Romanticism and achieved visual expression through the Arts and Crafts movement. Led by: Christian Dupont, Associate University Librarian for Scholarly Resources and Burns Librarian, Boston College In Celtic Art Across the Ages (March 6–August 2, 2026), discover the many forms of Celtic creativity and their artistic legacies in this sweeping story that spans ancient to modern times.

title: Harvard Art Museums at Night
description: Join us for an evening of art, fun, food, and more! This event is free and open to everyone. Gather with friends and mingle inside our Italian-inspired courtyard while taking in the smooth sounds from DJ C-Zone. Browse the museum shop and chat over a snack or drink for purchase from local vendors, such as Aeronaut Brewing Company. Stop by the Materials Lab for a fun art-making activity, and then drop in on one of our Spotlight Tours. You’ll also get the chance to win prizes! And of course, wander the galleries to take in our world-class art collections—over 50 galleries to explore! Don’t forget to check out our current exhibitions. Fiddler, Jenna Moynihan will also be performing during the evening! Harvard Art Museums at Night takes place the last Thursday of every month (holidays permitting), from 5 to 9pm. Each night features a new mix of local talent and community partners to make this a festive occasion for all. When arriving, enter via Quincy Street. In inclement weather, please use the Prescott entrance as it provides extra shelter. Advance registration is encouraged, but walk-in visitors are always welcome. Please note that space may be limited due to capacity. Registration opens two weeks before the event. Visit the museum website for the latest visitor policies and parking information. WBUR is the media partner for Harvard Art Museums at Night. This event is part of ArtsThursdays, a university-wide initiative supported by Harvard University Committee on the Arts (HUCA).

title: Gallery Performance: Celtic Art Across the Ages
description: Join us for a musical performance related to the special exhibition Celtic Art Across the Ages. Clare Fraser (fiddle) and Simon Lace (guitar/bouzouki) will play traditional Irish music and talk about Celtic musical heritage. In Celtic Art Across the Ages (March 6–August 2, 2026), discover the many forms of Celtic creativity and their artistic legacies in this sweeping story that spans ancient to modern times.

title: Materials Lab Workshop: Portable Personal Altars
description: This event is at capacity. An altar is a site for remembrance, devotion, or a meditation on what we want to attract into our life. Assembling objects and images draws attention to what we value and hold important. Join teaching artist Karen Jackson for a hands-on mixed media workshop in which she will guide you in making your own personal altar. Jackson will introduce the many forms of altars before sharing a variety of media and techniques you can use to enhance your altar’s interior and surface. Participants are invited to bring personal images or objects small enough to fit into a cigar box to incorporate into their creations.

title: Summer Spotlight Tour
description: Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours of the collections. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram at @harvardarthappens.

title: Gallery Talk: American Works of Art at the 250th
description: This event does not require registration; see further details below. From late January to early July 2026, curator of American art Horace D. Ballard will lead a series of gallery talks to coincide with the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Each talk will closely examine a work of art that speaks to the historical, social, and political contexts that continue to shape the events and ideas of the United States within the broader context of the colonial and political framework of the Americas. Please note that each month, the work of art experienced will change. This gallery talk is part of our New on View series, highlighting recent gallery installations and presenting new insights into recent acquisitions or old favorites. Led by: Horace D. Ballard, Theodore E. Stebbins, Jr., Curator of American Art, Division of European and American Art The Harvard Art Museums offer href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/plan-your-visit">free admission every day, Tuesday through Sunday. Please see the href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/general-policies">museum visit page to learn about our general policies for visiting the museums. edu">amregister@harvard.

title: Art Study Center Seminar: Jacques de Gheyn II
description: This talk follows the remarkable career of Jacques de Gheyn II, a Flemish-born draughtsman and printmaker who arrived in the Northern Netherlands in the 1590s as part of a broader wave of artists fleeing war and upheaval in the south. Looking at prints and drawings in the Art Study Center, we will explore what it took for artists to reinvent themselves in one of Europe’s most dynamic and rapidly changing art markets. Led by: Susanne Bartels, Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Curatorial Fellow, Division of European and American Art

title: Second Saturdays Story Time
description: Know Before You Go How to join: Check in at the Visitor Services desk in the Calderwood Courtyard. Fee: This is a free event. Age restrictions: Ages 3 to 7. Caregivers must be present with their children. Accessibility accommodations: Email href="mailto:amregister@harvard.edu">amregister@harvard.edu at least 48 hours in advance, including the name and date of the program in the subject line. General info: The href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/plan-your-visit">museum visit page has general guidelines for your visit. Join us for Second Saturdays Story Time in the galleries, an event in partnership with librarians from Cambridge, Somerville, Watertown, and Medford. In this wonderful, art-filled experience held every second Saturday of the month, librarians will choose thematic books to share with you and yours. This program is organized in partnership with the Cambridge Public Library, Somerville Public Library, Watertown Public Library, and Medford Public Library.

title: Gallery Performance: Celtic Art Across the Ages
description: In celebration of the special exhibition Celtic Art Across the Ages, Harvard student Samuel Puopolo will share some of his favorite Welsh medieval poetry, both in the original language and translated into English. Focusing on themes of resilience in the face of widespread change, these poems highlight the enduring cultural continuities of the Welsh as well as their deep-rooted commitment to poetry and song. Speaker: Samuel Puopolo, Ph.D. candidate in Celtic Languages and Literatures, Harvard University In Celtic Art Across the Ages (March 6–August 2, 2026), discover the many forms of Celtic creativity and their artistic legacies in this sweeping story that spans ancient to modern times.

title: Art + Science: Cotton Duck Canvas
description: This event does not require registration; see further details below. Have you ever wondered what happens in our conservation labs? Join a member of our Straus Center staff for an informal conversation about their work treating objects in our collections. Taking place just outside the Straus Center in the Lightbox Gallery, this presentation will give you the chance to get up close and hands-on with a selection of tools and materials used by conservation staff. In this session, associate paintings conservator href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/about/staff/284">Ellen Davis will talk about the use of cotton duck canvas. The Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies is a world leader in fine arts conservation, research, and training. The center’s laboratories are where conservation, conservation science, and curatorial practice intersect, coming together to enrich the understanding of and care for the approximately 250,000 objects in the Harvard Art Museums collections. Space is limited, and this program is available on a first-come, first-served basis; no registration is required. The Harvard Art Museums offer href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/plan-your-visit">free admission every day, Tuesday through Sunday. Please see the href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/general-policies">museum visit page to learn about our general policies for visiting the museums.

title: Exhibition Tour: Celtic Art Across the Ages
description: Go behind the scenes to learn more about the design, production, and installation of the special exhibition Celtic Art Across the Ages, with exhibition designer Robert Checchi. description: Join us for an evening of art, fun, food, and more! Gather with friends and mingle inside our spectacular Italian-inspired courtyard, evoking the energy of a bustling town piazza. DJ C-Zone will set the mood with smooth, curated sounds as you chat, snack, sip, and catch up over bites and drinks available for purchase from local vendors. Drop in on a Spotlight Tour, browse the museum shop, and stop by the Materials Lab for a fun art-making activity. title: Summer Spotlight Tour
description: Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours of the collections. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram at @harvardarthappens.

title: Gray Area: Compassion and Companionship
description: The 14th-century tale of Saint Roch (Rocco) and his canine companion recounts the pair’s selfless compassion and care for those suffering. Join us to explore how today, amid global challenges such as pandemics and social isolation, the story serves as a reminder of the importance of humanitarian values and solidarity. This talk is part of Gray Area, a series that features members of our staff exploring artworks that capture the complexities of humanity, political landscapes, ethics, ideologies, power dynamics, and critical thinking in our times. Through this series, we hope to encourage people to observe and consider their own individual gray areas, and to think about how their unique experiences guide the choices they make. Led by: Jeanne Burke, Academic and Public Programs Coordinator, Division of Academic and Public Programs

title: Art + Science: Materials and Techniques in Frame Conservation
description: This event does not require registration; see further details below. Have you ever wondered what happens in our conservation labs? Join a member of our Straus Center staff for an informal conversation about their work treating objects in our collections. Taking place just outside the Straus Center in the Lightbox Gallery, this presentation will give you the chance to get up close and hands-on with a selection of tools and materials used by conservation staff. In this session, associate frames conservator href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/about/staff/230">Allison Jackson will talk about materials and techniques in frame conservation. The Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies is a world leader in fine arts conservation, research, and training. The center’s laboratories are where conservation, conservation science, and curatorial practice intersect, coming together to enrich the understanding of and care for the approximately 250,000 objects in the Harvard Art Museums collections. Space is limited, and this program is available on a first-come, first-served basis; no registration is required. The Harvard Art Museums offer href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/plan-your-visit">free admission every day, Tuesday through Sunday. Please see the href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/general-policies">museum visit page to learn about our general policies for visiting the museums.

Each intern will focus on a single object in the collections that they’ve selected and researched. A brief question and answer period will follow each talk. There will be two hour-long sessions offered, one at 11am and one at 2pm. Feel free to attend both programs! Also, check out other projects teens have built at the museums in previous years.

title: Afmohip: Traveling Village
description: Under the direction of Mrs. JoJo Caidor, Afmohip proudly presents our first-ever full evening-length show, Traveling Village. A work rooted in the past, present, community, and connections.Traveling Village is a sequel that represents communities from different ethnic groups, paving the way and creating connections between the past and the present. It shows the beginnings of shared resources and mutual support, leading to the collective power found in solidarity. The strength of a single, shared force brings unison, togetherness, and courage. It acknowledges that struggles existed before and continue today, while reminding us of the reasons behind our current way of life. At its core, it emphasizes the importance of receiving, understanding, and sharing, allowing communities to endure and grow.

title: ☀️ Summer Series: Samba & Latin Dance Party
description: A high-energy night of live music and dance rooted in Latin and Brazilian traditions featuring Receita de Samba & Friends. This festive evening invites audiences to move, celebrate, and experience the rhythms that connect cultures across the Americas.

title: ☀️ Summer Series: The Summer Throwdown
description: The Summer Series concludes with The Summer Throwdown, MC’ed by the legendary Megatron, a high-energy end-of-season celebration featuring DJs, live performances, and an electrifying dance battle. This event brings the community together one final time to close out the summer with music and movement.

title: Yarumi González: Artist in Residence Showcase
description: The Artist in Residence Showcase celebrates the culmination of MAC’s residency program, highlighting works developed through sustained artistic exploration and experimentation. Rather than focusing solely on finished pieces, the showcase invites audiences into the creative process, offering a glimpse into evolving ideas and artistic discovery. MAC is honored to announce this year’s Artist in Residence, Yarumi González. During her residency, González will continue developing a multidisciplinary, autobiographical work exploring identity, migration, and the American Dream through poetic and ritual-inspired storytelling, movement, video, photography, installation, and performance.

title: Lift Every Voice: BIPOC Play Festival
description: A signature MAC program, Lift Every Voice amplifies the work of BIPOC playwrights, poets, and spoken word artists through staged readings and performances. The festival creates space for artists to share new work while fostering meaningful dialogue between creators and audiences.

title: Día de los Muertos Celebration
description: Honoring the rich Mexican tradition of Día de los Muertos, this immersive community celebration features music, dance, storytelling, and altar installations that invite audiences to reflect on ancestry, remembrance, and the enduring bonds between generations.

title: Barbed Wire
description: Each year we celebrate MLK – the person and the weekend – with a performance focused on the legacy of Black America from Civil Rights to today. This year we bring to the stage Barbed Wire, a new work presented in full for the first time on our stage.

title: The Fabric of Us: A Celebration of Black Fashion Through the Decades
description: This annual showcase celebrates the evolution of Black style, identity, and cultural expression across generations. Through original designs inspired by movements ranging from the Harlem Renaissance to contemporary fashion culture, the event highlights the lasting influence of Black creativity and innovation.

title: MAC Movement Makers: The M³ Festival
description: A new addition to MAC’s programming, MAC Movement Makers: The M³ Festival is a multi-day celebration of contemporary dance and movement-based performance. Bringing together choreographers, performers, and audiences, the festival creates opportunities for artistic experimentation, collaboration, and dialogue while expanding MAC’s presence within the dance community.Across the season, MAC continues to deepen its investment in artist development, signature cultural programming, and community-centered experiences that position the organization as both a creative incubator and a gathering place for diverse communities.Each performance will include the works of two dance companies, followed by a Q+A with one company.Tickets to individual performances are $40Choose tickets to any two performances, and receive 25% off your order!Choose tickets to all four performances, and receive 50% off your order!

title: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Macbeth *Special 2-hr Touring Edition!*
description: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Macbeth *Special 2-hr Touring Edition!* “By the pricking of my thumbs, something wicked [tipsy] this way comes” Shakespeare’s tale of murder, ambition, bloodlust, and the supernatural. Bloody Macbeth and his murderous wife Lady M seize the Scottish throne- what could stop them other than a few shots and some poorly poured beer? When presented by Shit-faced Shakespeare NO ONE can predict the ending! Content Curious? Our shows feature murder, treason, war, violence (personal, sexual, and national), suicide, regicide, incest, and blasphemy- and that is just the Shakespeare! Our drinker has been known to contribute profanity, and the occasionally bare butt-cheek. If any of this puts you off, maybe another show is more your speed. Warning: Our show does engage flashing lights and loud noises. Also, for those choosing to sit close to the stage- there is the possibility of splashing beer and being a part of the show. About Shit-faced Shakespeare® An entirely serious Shakespeare play, with an entirely shit-faced cast member The original, award winning, international smash-hit direct from London’s West End to an American theater near you! Founded in 2010 in the UK and first arriving on US shores back in 2015. Shit-faced Shakespeare® has delighted audiences all over the States with their highfalutin cocktail of traditional Elizabethan theater and balls-to-the-wall drunken shenanigans. Accept no poor relations, pale imitations or paltry recreations, see the authentic Shit-faced Shakespeare® show which started it all. Featuring a revolving cast of Boston’s finest actors, the choicest cuts of Shakespearian classics and more inebriated antics than you can violently shake a cod piece at. Shit-faced Shakespeare® is the unique theatrical experience that has left audiences roaring in the aisles the world over. Age Limit: Fridays are 18+ and Saturdays are 21+ Doors 6:15 PM Show 7:00 PM – 9:00 PM including a 15 minute intermission

title: Lectures On Tap: Cinematic Storytelling: Visual Structure in Film
description: Lectures On Tap: Cinematic Storytelling: Visual Structure in Film Event Description: Join us for an engaging evening as Prof. Drew McClellan unpacks how filmmakers communicate thoughts, emotions, and ideas through visual strategy and cinematic design. You’ll discover how every shot is carefully constructed to guide your emotions, deepen storytelling, and choreograph the eye across the frame. Through close analysis of still images and iconic scenes from classic and contemporary cinema, this lecture reveals the “secret” visual language used by directors, cinematographers, production designers, and editors to shape and enhance the audience experience. Whether you’re a filmmaker, film lover, designer, student, or simply curious about why movies “feel” the way they do, this session offers an accessible and inspiring look at the architecture of cinematic storytelling—and will forever change the way you watch films. Drew McClellan is an award-winning educator, filmmaker, and visual strategist whose work focuses on the intersection of cinematic storytelling and visual strategy. He serves as an adjunct professor at the USC School of Cinematic Arts and is currently Chair of the Cinematic Arts Department at the Los Angeles County High School for the Arts (LACHSA). title: Commedia Dell’Arte: The Mastery of Mask & Physical Comedy with Mycah Hogan
description: Commedia Dell’Arte: The Mastery of Mask & Physical Comedy with Mycah Hogan Step into the vibrant, high-stakes, and highly stupid world of Commedia dell’Arte in this immersive two-day intensive. Designed for actors, educators, and anyone who’s mask-curious, thiis workshop aims to strip away the “polite” performer to reveal the raw, hilarious, and wildly human archetypes that have fueled comedy for centuries. Participants will explore the rigorous physicality and spontaneous play required to bring the iconic stock characters—Arlecchino, Capitano, Pantalone, Dottore, and others — to life. Through mask work, ensemble devising, and the study of lazzi (classic comedic business), you’ll learn how to activate these characters in your own body and build authentic (and sometimes surprising) connections to the audience. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your comedic timing, expand your physical range, or simply reclaim a sense of wonder in your craft, this weekend is about unlocking the power of the mask. title: A Moment To Spare
description: A Moment To Spare A Moment to Spare is an interactive comedy show telling a story about a fool (me, Colin) arriving at an existential crossroads after the death of his father (How cliché, I know right?). He and the audience wind up getting sucked into the video game of his life where the objective is simple – rewrite the past so he can be “perfect” in the future. Oh, and just a heads up – he will need your help. If all goes well, this could fix him and probably change the world as we know it. It’s part clown show, part stand-up, and part narrative storytelling where the audience gets a say in how the story gets told. Bio: Colin is a comedian and writer who’s performed in theaters all over the country. title: Thom Tran
description: Thom Tran Thom Tran is a Los Angeles–based comedian, actor, musician, and U.S. Army combat veteran whose stand-up career began after surviving a gunshot wound to the back of the head while deployed to Iraq. Following his medical retirement, Tran relocated to Los Angeles in 2008 and quickly immersed himself in the comedy scene. He went on to found The GIs of Comedy, an internationally touring, all-military veteran stand-up group that has performed for U.S. service members stationed and deployed in combat zones worldwide. The group was featured on Larry Charles’ Dangerous World of Comedy (Netflix) and has appeared on CBS and NBC. As a solo act, Tran tours nationally and internationally, including dates across Europe with longtime collaborator Brad Williams, performing in Denmark, Norway, England, Ireland, and beyond. His material blends sharp observational humor with lived experience, delivered with discipline and timing honed both on stage and in service. Based in Hollywood, Tran is a regular at premier clubs including the World Famous Laugh Factory and the Comedy & Magic Club, in addition to theaters and venues throughout Southern California. On screen, Tran has co-starred on NCIS: Los Angeles and SEAL Team (CBS) and appears in the feature film My Dead Friend Zoe alongside Morgan Freeman, Sonequa Martin-Green, and Ed Harris. title: Experimental Sketch Workshop with Andy Miara
description: Experimental Sketch Workshop with Andy Miara If you’re a sketch writer, performer, director or teacher who is interested in process, experimentation and discovery, this workshop is for you! This full day session will operate like a professional sketch rehearsal with a focus on material generation and productive exploration. Through writing, improvisation and on-our-feet exercises, we’ll play with a range of techniques to create material. A comfort with improvisation is a plus. Come ready to play and let’s see what we can make together! ABOUT ANDY: Andy Miara is a former director for The Second City in Chicago where he also served as a core writing instructor in the Second City Training Center. He is a former head writer of The Onion News Network and co-creator of The Onion’s sister site, Clickhole.com. Alongside Tim Robinson and Mark Raterman, Miara co-founded the sketch group My Mans. The trio developed pilots for Comedy Central and Adult Swim, and created The Thanksgiving House, an immersive theater show in Los Angeles produced by Funny or Die and IFC. Miara has written on animated comedies including Robot Chicken and SuperMansion, and has developed original projects with NBC, TBS, truTV, and Cartoon Network. Most recently, he co-wrote and directed the scripted audio series Get It To Dutch for iHeart Media, and currently has an animated pilot in development at Fox starring Tim Robinson and Cecily Strong. title: Wrestling with the Written Word: A Clown & Physical Theatre Workshop with Sheriden Thomas
description: Wrestling with the Written Word: A Clown & Physical Theatre Workshop with Sheriden Thomas SHOW DESCRIPTION: It is, and is not the words. It’s the situation. You, your partner(s), and imagination in the moment are the situation…. We will be fooling around with written words, using the Dynamics, the Complicities, the Clown Personas, and the Tension States, as a fruitful path for mining the physical and the fun. Very brief texts of Will Shakespeare & Sam Beckett will be supplied…. And you can bring your own. A monologue, a scene, a poem, a manifesto. It’s all grist, darlin’. ARTIST BIO: Over several decades, Sheriden has acted under Actor’s Equity Contracts in the nation’s regional theatres. Starting in the 70’s, playing ingénues for the Guthrie Theatre in Minneapolis to Boston’s Moonbox Productions, garnering a Boston Critics Award for Kimberly in Kimberly Akimbo. Recently, in film, she played two old ladies. One in Tiffany Paulson’s About Fate and another in Eric Aronson’s Any Day Now about the Gardner Museum heist. It’s now streaming on Amazon Prime. Sheriden has directed and taught acting at Cornell and Southern Methodist Universities. Since arriving in Boston, she directed plays and readings for Another Country, Queer Soup Productions, and Boston Playwrights’ Theatre. As Senior Lecturer Emerita, at Tufts University, she taught a variety of acting courses including Advanced Acting Lab, Shakespeare, Mask, Physical Comedy, and Acting as Career. She directed a dozen plays, concluding with an edited video of Jeffrey Hatcher’s delightfully, silly adaptation of The Government Inspector. Sheriden has directed professionally for the Shakespeare Festival of Dallas, Mother Jones in Chicago, Company Theatre in Los Angeles, Manhattan Class, and WOW Cafe in New York City. She will be directing The Beauty Queen of Leenane for Theater Uncorked this November at Boston Center for the Arts. Her Tufts bio is: https://tdps.tufts.edu/people/faculty/sheriden-thomas Doors: 10:45 AM Start

title: Bubble Burlesque: Denim Diaspora
description: Bubble Burlesque: Denim Diaspora Step into a world where rebellion meets rhinestones, and fabric tells a story far deeper than fashion. Denim & Desire is a burlesque experience that peels back the seams of history, celebrating denim not just as an icon of style, but as a symbol woven through Black resilience, labor, culture, and expression. From its roots as durable workwear worn by enslaved and working class Black laborers, to its transformation into a global statement of cool shaped by Black musicians, dancers, and tastemakers, denim has always carried more than meets the eye. August 16th, we honor that legacy, thread by thread, strip by strip. Expect a dazzling lineup of performers who will reimagine denim in all its forms, raw, rugged, glamorous, and subversive. Through tease, storytelling, and unapologetic sensuality, each act pays tribute to the Black bodies and voices that turned denim into a canvas of identity and power. This is more than a show. It is a reclamation. A celebration. A strut through history in your best blues. So grab your seats, hold onto your hems, and get ready to witness denim like you have never seen it before. Denim is in our genes. From our enslaved ancestors dressed in negro cloth, to the denim clad cowboys on dude ranches, to denim being reclaimed and made into a statement of rebellion in the civil rights movement, to the repositioning of denim in the world of fashion due in part to black taste makers. On August 16th at The Rockwell, join Bubble Burlesque and an Iconic all black cast to find out how we continue to set your tongue. Lyrically, these tunes work through issues of identity, boundaries, long distance relationships, short distance situationships, and the flux of family. title: “Be Good” with Paulette
description: “Be Good” with Paulette OH LOOK! HERE COMES THE MILDEST MAN IMAGINABLE. Paulette stumbles into a room full of the most strangers he’s ever seen, and he doesn’t know whether to panic or mingle—so he does both, for 60 minutes. Sporting a brown sweater and a hot-off-the-fist black eye, he dares to address the room armed with nothing but an arsenal of pleasantries and a monumental fear of rejection. Hot off of a high octane tour of Europe, the UK, and even the east coast of America, certified clown Daniel Maseda brings well-mannered idiot Paulette back to The Rockwell for the very second time with this fan-favorite show that never plays out the same way twice. A perfect evening for anyone who wants to scream at a polite person. title: Cambridge Cooks: Caribbean Heritage Month Edition with Chef Gaitskell (Main)
description: Join Chef Gaitskell Cleghorn Jr. as he prepares Jerk Chicken and Mango Salsa in celebration of Caribbean-American Heritage Month. Gaitskell Cleghorn Jr., professionally known as Chef Gates, is an entrepreneur and culinary educator based in Boston. He specializes in culinary education, catering, and community outreach, partnering with organizations such as the Codman Square Farmers Market and BOLD Teens. Throughout his career, he has taught at prestigious institutions, including Harvard University, as well as local schools such as Madison Park Technical Vocational High School and Boston Day & Evening Academy. His work has been featured in publications including Channel 7, Edible Boston, Boston Herald, and the Boston Globe. Additionally, he collaborated with a Master Sushi Chef to produce over 3,000 sushi plates at the New England Seafood Expo. His work on food and culture is currently featured in an Exhibit at the Boston Children’s Museum. Although he lived globally due to his father’s military service, he has spent most of his professional life in Boston, where he continues to grow as a culinary professional.

title: Acrylic Painting Workshop (Valente)
description: Learn how to create beautiful and colorful acrylic paintings! In this class you will be introduced to painting with acrylic, including techniques in color mixing, observational painting, and composition. At your own pace you will learn how to paint still lifes using acrylic paint in a relaxed and welcoming environment. This class will cover wet on wet and wet and dry brush techniques, sgraffito/combing, overlays/glazing, gel mediums, pattern making, and masking. You will come away from this class with beautiful paintings of your own and a greater understanding and appreciation for the medium of acrylic painting. Registration Required. This class is suitable for beginners and can be adjusted for all levels of experience. This class is taught by Brooke Lambert. Brooke is a professional printmaker and painter. She holds a BFA from Massachusetts College of Art and Design and shows her work widely in New England, New York, and beyond. Brooke works in Studio 291 at Western Avenue Studios & Lofts in Lowell, MA. She is currently represented by The Society of American Graphic Artists and Equity Gallery in New York, NY and Galaray House, contemporary art gallery in Lexington, MA. She has thirteen years of teaching experience and currently teaches adult art workshops and holds artist demos at several locations in New England.

description: In this 90-minute workshop, you’ll learn the basics of sewing machine operation and safety. This session will cover machine setup, basic functions, threading the machine, reloading the bobbin, sewing straight stitches, and recognizing when stitch tension has gone awry. As we learn together, we’ll work on a simple sewing project—a drawstring bag—which most students will be able to complete by the end of the class. You must complete Hive Safety Training before registering for this workshop. If you have not completed the training, you will be removed from the class—even if you plan to take it later. title: Bruce Gertz Quintet
description: $15 / $10 students / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated Bruce's new solo recordings are like meditations that vibrate in the solar plexus and resonate through your being. His command of the instrument and imagination are an elixir for being transported to the pure music channel. Bravo Bruce - Jerry Bergonzi Every morning, world-renowned jazz bassist, composer, and educator, Bruce Gertz, makes himself a cup of coffee and sits at the baby grand piano of his Melrose, MA living room. Surrounded by quirky plants, records of his esteemed inspirations, and albums of his own, Gertz composes something every day, regardless of the day’s events ahead. He says, "Sometimes I only get a short idea but that can be the seed of a beautiful composition." His counterparts applaud him for his restless commitment to self-improvement. Gertz is known for his superb mastery of the upright bass and was named “Outstanding Bassist” by Boston Music Awards. What some fans don’t know is that he grew up playing electric bass from the age of 14 and still plays (and teaches) the electric quite often. His extraordinary contribution to music education has earned him multiple recognition awards from The International Association of Jazz Educators and the Jazz Education Network. He has been serving as a Professor of Bass at Berklee College of Music since 1976. Additional educator credits include serving on the advisory board of the International Society of Bassists and as an adjudicator at the Clark Terry UNH Jazzer's Festival. Gertz has performed and recorded with such artists as Gary Burton, Jerry Bergonzi, John Abercrombie, Joey Calderazzo, Kenny Werner, Mick Goodrick, Kurt Rosenwinkel, Billy Hart, Bill Frisell, Bob Berg, George Cables, Gil Evans, Tom Harrell, Jon Hendricks, Diane Schuur, Dave Brubeck, George Garzone, Mike Stern, Larry Coryell, Joe Lovano, Cab Calloway, Maynard Ferguson, Count Basie and many others. title: Gill Aharon Trio
description: Inspired by the cartoon music of the 50s and 60s, the drive of Led Zeppelin, the genius and humor of Frank Zappa, the perfection of Bach, the relentlessness of Ligeti, the courage of Medeski, Martin and Wood, the jam of Phish live, the beauty of the Beatles and the immersive nature of music, I am in pursuit of truth through music. “Sometimes I think of us musicians as kids playing in order to learn how to be adults, but we can just keep playing. The game of playing music together is too much fun to make it work. With that in mind, I refuse to write arrangements. I never want my friends and bandmates to feel obliged to do anything. - Gill Aharon

title: Improbable Beasts Album Release Show
description: Suggested donation $10-$40 / 7:30 doors / 8pm start / seated & standing The Improbable Beasts bass clarinet ensemble is releasing not one but TWO live albums, and we're celebrating with a performance of all the tunes! After several years of performing, we've accumulated a nice collection of live performance recordings. We've selected some of our very best ones, mixed and mastered them to perfection, and now we are releasing them into the wild! At the show, the new albums will be available for discounted purchase in CD form, as well as lots of other fun merchandise: t-shirts, stickers, caps, and tattoos. Come on out to party and celebrate with the Improbable Beasts!

title: Newfane Record Release Party
description: free admission / 10pm doors / 10:30 start / standing Newfane is a 4-piece indie rock band from Boston. Their new record, "All Goodbyes Are Lies," is out in 2026. Their influences include REM, Wilco, Sebadoh, and Queens of the Stone Age. The band has a song in Rock Band 4 and got radio play on WMBR's Pipeline and Boston Emissions. They've had shows at the Lizard Lounge, Sally O'Brien's, Plough and Stars, Midway Cafe, and Atwood's.

title: Whiskey Ginger w/ Cogs and Parachute Club
description: $10 advance / $12 day of show / 7pm doors / 7:30 show Whiskey Ginger is on tour in anticipation of the release of their debut album. Whiskey Ginger is a four piece indie rock outfit that’s bold yet unassuming, striking a balance between raw energy and effortlessly cool. initially started as a solo project by singer/songwriter emily pitcairn, it has grown into a dynamic and distinctive band featuring lyle rea on drums and mia peach on bass.

title: Hidden Fountain / Trabants / Children of the Flaming Wheel at the Lilypad
description: a night of kaleidoscopic freakouts, exploratory surf-rock and electric dreamscapes Hidden Fountain is an easy-listening synthesizer demonstration by Aaron Bennett (Planet of Adventure, Crystal Understanding), Chris Braiotta (Shitaly, Planet of Adventure), Noell Dorsey (Major Stars, Violet Nox), and Kathleen Mahoney (Kathy Snax, Adult Learners). Named after the diminutive and once ubiquitous Eastern European automobile, Trabants (pronounced Truh-bonts) is a rotating line-up of musicians fronted by composer/guitarist Eric Penna who find their muse in the dusty bins of 60's beat records. They play an instrumental mix of vintage-inspired surf, garage and psych with a cinematic twist. Children of the Flaming Wheel plays galapagogo garage punk for the freakazoids!

title: Elan Mehler Trio
description: Elan Mehler has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat. His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press. Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival. In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night.Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world. title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: Jerry Bergonzi, Tenor Saxophone A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

title: The Fringe
description: The Fringe originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist George Garzone, bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist John Lockwood. Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums, graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. George Garzone, Tenor Saxophone Lineup subject to change without notice

title: Bert Seager's Heart of Hearing
description: $15 suggested / $5 with Student ID / 6:30pm start / seated Bert Seager’s Heart of Hearing is a-jazz quartet made up of piano, tenor-saxophone, upright-bass, and drums whose aim is to bring listeners into the heart of improvised jazz. The joyful expression of this musical intimacy, the shimmering transparency of the sound, and the sense that these musicians are as much involved in listening as in playing makes for compelling and memorable performances.

title: Bevan Manson Trio ft. Allan Chase
description: $20 at the door / $15 advance / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated 35 years after the release of their underground hit "Rhythm Chowder", pianist/composer Bevan Manson, drummer Matt Wilson and bassist Bob Nieske reunite to play their unique, unpredictable and deeply felt renditions of jazz standards and originals. Saxophonist Allan Chase joins as special guest on a night that marks a full circle moment in Boston jazz history. Here’s a link to their recording “Rhythm Chowder” Bevan Manson has received composing commissions from Sierra Chamber Music, Pacific Philharmonic Foundation, the San Francisco Symphony, clarinetist Gary Gray, the Channel Islands Chamber Orchestra and LACO violist Victoria Miskolczy amongst others. Recently an arranger for Manhattan Transfer vocalist Cheryl Bentyne’s Sondheim album, Mr. Manson has also arranged music for Village Vanguard Orchestra saxophonist Gary Smulyan and L.A. vocalist Cathy Segal Garcia. ​Currently a free-lance composer/arranger and jazz pianist in L.A. and points west, he has been a faculty member at New England Conservatory, Director of UC Jazz at UC Berkeley and jazz faculty at Ventura College. He has also worked in the L.A. film and TV industries. Bevan’s classical works have been recorded on Albany Records; he has a recent jazz release of his on Meistero Music ’The Jazz Cave’. Other recordings have been released on Iris Records and Challenge (Netherlands). Matt Wilson has released thirteen albums as a leader, appeared on morethan 400 others as a sideman and has played with an impressive array of some of the most legendary names in jazz, including Wynton Marsalis, Lee Konitz, Joe Lovano, Pat Metheny, Dewey Redman, Charlie Haden, John Scofield, Joanne Brackeen and Herbie Hancock, just to name a few. title: Sophie Wellington Album Release + Square Dance!
description: $20 admission / 7:30 doors / 8pm start / seated & standing Celebrate the release of Sophie's new album, Her Bright Smile Haunts Me Still with a intimate and guitar forward solo set, followed by a celebratory square dance! Her Bright Smile Haunts Me Still is Sophie's second album, and it focuses on how to approach playing guitar like a fiddler, singer, and percussive dancer. She uses alternate guitar tunings and "fiddle picking" techniques to emulate the feel and sound of the fiddle. She accompanies her voice using harmonic gravity, rhythmic velocity, and her experience as a ballad singer and jazz vocalist. HBSHMS is artfully recorded, mixed, and produced by Grammy Award winning artist Cathy Fink. Live tracked and performed solo, it is a souvenir of Sophie's dynamic musicianship. Sophie Wellington is an old time fiddler, flatpick guitarist, percussive dancer and jazz vocalist based in Boston, MA. Sophie grew up in Staunton, VA and was raised in its vibrant music community by musician and dance caller Bill Wellington and classical pianist Lynne Mackey. Sophie graduated from Berklee College of Music in 2022 with a degree in jazz voice and American roots music, and has since taught fiddle, flatfooting, guitar, and music theory at numerous festivals and camps. Sophie also toured extensively with musician and modern day bard Willi Carlisle.

title: h2 Live @ The Lilypad
description: $10 cover / 10pm doors / 10:30 start / seated & standing h2, the fusion project of violinist and composer Luke Norman, plays original compositions and arrangements from their debut EP, “Running Late”. The performance features Luke Norman on violin, Angelo Della Valle on guitar, Anderson Mirafzali on bass, and Nick White on drums. h2 is a Boston-based fusion artist whose music bridges the worlds of jazz, electronic, and experimental rock. His music combines intricate melodies with high-octane grooves that exemplify precision, depth, and a forward-thinking approach to fusion. Drawing inspiration from Mahavishnu Orchestra, Ghost Note, and Machine Girl, his music bridges the analog warmth of classic fusion with the freneticism of contemporary electronic music.

title: Reconnecting Rivers Screening at Portico Brewing
description: Raise a glass for restored rivers! Join the CRWA Young Professionals Board at Portico Brewing to learn about our ongoing work to restore a clean, resilient Charles River for future generations. At 6:45PM, we will screen the short film “Reconnecting Rivers,” produced by CRWA and Turnaround Films in 2026 to highlight the challenges posed by defunct dams and how we are working to address them. A brief Q&A will follow the screening. Enjoy Portico’s re-release of our delicious collaboration beer Dam Free Ale while you watch!

title: Pixel Party
description: Build a wooden model of an iconic Nintendo character! Each participant will be given a set of painted wooden blocks that correspond with their chosen character. You will then be guided step by step on how to glue the blocks together to make a wooden model of a character from the 8-bit era of gaming. All materials will be provided and no experience is necessary. Final sculptures will vary in size. The tallest is Samus (13 inches) and the shortest are Mario & Link (each 6.7 inches). If you do not finish your sculpture during the event, you are welcome to take everything you need to finish it at home. If you would like to build a character that is not listed in the dropdown menu, feel free to email robertpatricklynch@gmail.com with requests. This is an all ages event. Children under 13 should be signed up at their parent/guardian's discretion. They will need adult supervision and have the ability to sit and do a project for 1-2 hours without being disruptive.

title: Somerville Fermentation Festival
description: A celebration of food and culture in Somerville, MA The Somerville Fermentation Festival brings together a community of fermented food & beverage vendors, passionate enthusiasts, and anyone curious to learn more about fermentation in a one-day celebration of the world of fermented foods. Sample a diverse range of ferments, learn how to make your own sauerkraut, swap starter cultures with other local fermenters, and attend presentations by experts in the field.

title: Bill Blumenreich Presents: Chill Towards Enlightenment: A Stoke Seminar with Chad Goes Deep
description: A satirical ted talk seminar on his stoke philosophy where he tackles the question: “Why is bummer so prevalent in our society and how do we transcend it?” Join us on this beautiful journey and learn Chad’s transformative technique, The Chill Method, which will help you reclaim your inner joy and set you on a new path to enjoy this radical adventure we call life.

title: The Moth: Boston StorySLAM - HOLIDAY GONE WRONG
description: Join us the fourth Tuesday of each month for the Boston Moth StorySLAM! This community-focused, open-mic storytelling competition is open to anyone can share a story on the night’s theme (changes every month). HOLIDAY GONE WRONG: Five-minute stories about vacation woes. The moments you wished you could click your heels and be back home to the times you had to McGyver your way through. Stolen passports, lost reservations, the unsung hero that saved the day. Desert mirages, dead batteries, dangerous encounters. It was about the journey, not the destination. 6:30pm Doors Open | 7:30pm Stories Begin

title: Dungeons & Dragons Heroes Quest Day Camps (Morning Sessions)
description: LARP Adventure Program invites young heroes to dive into the world of tabletop role-playing games with our Dungeons & Dragons Summer Day Camp! Grab your dice, bring your imagination, and get ready for a summer full of heroic choices and unforgettable stories! In this imaginative, story-driven experience, players will build skills in creativity, teamwork, critical thinking, math, and public speaking—all while having a blast. Using Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition, our friendly, experienced staff will guide students step by step through creating their own characters and embarking on exciting adventures filled with puzzles, challenges, and epic storytelling. Role-playing games give players experience with a variety of skills, including improvisation, critical thinking, math, and public speaking. Our staff will be using Dungeons and Dragons 5th Edition rules to guide participants through the process of creating characters and then testing their might through an interactive story. Students are taught at a comfortable skill level how to make characters and even run their own games as dungeon masters.

title: A Cell Phone Movie - screening
description: Struggling, out of work actor Will Sterling made a feature film entirely on his cell phone about a fictional version of himself, a similarly struggling, out of work actor making a movie on his cell phone about a struggling, out of work actor making a movie on his cell phone. The result is “A Cell Phone Movie,” a $20k micro-budget meta-comedy that’s just as chaotic as it is self aware. Nominated for best debut at Raindance, it blurs the lines between reality and fiction as it explores artistic obsession, failing on purpose, and refusing to give up on a dream. The screening includes a live introduction by Sterling and a post film talk that’s part stand-up comedy, part motivational shove to inspire you to get out there and make the d*mn thing!

Alphabet is a youth contemporary circus show about what past generations leave behind—and what the next generation chooses to believe in.

title: Camp in Motion
description: How does “camp” function in The Mystery of Irma Vep? Charles Ludlam’s play is full of drag, excess, theatrical artifice, and comic transformation, but camp is never only style. Seen from the present, Irma Vep asks new questions about gender performance, theatrical instability, and what camp continues to make possible. As camp has shifted since the 1980s, so too have the critical frameworks audiences bring to a work like this one. What does Ludlam’s play reveal now, and what does it ask us to notice differently?

title: Ludlam After Ludlam
description: What has Charles Ludlam come to mean in the decades since his death? The Mystery of Irma Vep has historically been treated as the best-known entry point into his work, but it is also part of a much larger, queer theatrical legacy, one that has been reshaped by changing artists, audiences, and performance cultures. To look at Ludlam now is to ask not only who he was, but how he has been inherited.

title: Costuming Camp: Transformation on Stage
description: With only two actors playing a whole world of characters, The Mystery of Irma Vep depends on costumes that are fast, flexible, and thrilling. How do you design for that kind of transformation while also capturing the play’s camp, humor, and Gothic excess? Stay after the show for a conversation with costume designer Seth Bodie on the challenges and pleasures of dressing Ludlam’s whirlwind of roles.

title: The Mystery of Irma Vep
description: A quick-change, creepy, campy cult classic! Two actors play all the roles – from household servants to a vampire mummy – in this affectionate send-up of Gothic novels, B-horror movies, and English drawing room comedies. A howling good time filled with werewolves, ghosts, and more plot twists than you can shake a wooden stake at.

title: Staging the Ridiculous & Costuming Camp
description:
Join us for a post-show conversation with director and scenic designer David R. Gammons and costume designer Seth Bodie that explores the process, challenges and pleasures of directing and costuming one of Charles Ludlam’s most beloved plays, The Mystery of Irma Vep.

What does it take to direct a play so invested in transformation, excess, and illusion, and how does one shape its camp surface into a coherent theatrical world? What are the challenges and pleasures of capturing Irma Vep’s camp, humor, and Gothic excess with costumes that are fast, flexible, and thrilling? Find out after the 7:30 show.
